findings: Previously canonical-string Ordinal keys could not import raw session card_type aliases: uppercase entries missed canonical card queries, and later aliases did not replace earlier deadlines. Three new regression cases fail before the fix and all pass afterwards.

Blacklist storage now uses private symbolic FName identity: truncate at UTF16 NUL, parse eligible ASCII numeric suffix, handle empty/None and1024-unit base substitution, fold only ASCII A-Z and retain all other UTF16 units. Symbolic base and Number are compared ordinally; allocation indices are not reproduced.

Constructor, explicit logical-map Load, session merge and query share key conversion. Last equivalent entry wins in input order; signed inclusive deadlines, valid/connected gates, old-map retention, immutability and cache invalidation are retained. Canonical callers remain compatible.

The oracle fixture is generated by executing captured current native code in an isolated successful synthetic pool.81 strings form44 identity groups, including empty/None/Number, ASCII/nonASCII, NUL and1023/1024/1025 base boundaries. C# tests compare every6561 pair, all2019 card aliases and warmed Develop candidate updates; Release594/594 passes.
limits: Symbolic equality models successful mode1 UTF16 conversion for blacklisting only. It does not emulate client allocation IDs, original display spelling, locks, memory failure, fatal limits or initialization. No client functions or live writes are used.

Actual session/world selection, automatic acquisition, retry/refresh/clearing lifecycle and concurrent mutation remain unaudited. No replay is used as authority, and no full card semantics is certified.
